what: The map says the proof-plan model is 'tuned' but also says nothing is retrained, and the landing FAQ answers 'Yes' to 'Is the model really tuned on my work?'. The claim is stronger than the method described on the page.
expected: Use wording that matches the method (for example 'voice profile and examples in context, not retrained') everywhere the word 'tuned' appears, or change the method.
evidence: Map card label '2. Tuned model' with body 'How it is tuned: voice profile + examples in context. Nothing is retrained.'; landing FAQ: 'Is the model really tuned on my work? Yes, in context: ...'; landing pricing card: 'your tuned model'.

what: Unknown URLs return HTTP 200 and render the Clerk sign-in card instead of a not-found page. Search engines and users get no real 404 for mistyped paths.
expected: Unknown routes return HTTP 404 with a not-found page that offers the career map.
evidence: Walk step not-found-pages: 'unknown page status 200' (FAIL). Screenshot shows 'Sign in to My AI Skill Tutor'. Unknown map token returns 404 correctly ('We couldn't find that map').

what: The primary header and hero button say 'Browse Talent Pool' while the same hero says the talent pool is not open yet.
expected: Primary CTA matches availability, for example 'Join as a candidate' or a waitlist label.
evidence: Hero text: 'The talent pool is opening soon. Join as a candidate'; buttons: 'Browse Talent Pool' (hero and header).

what: Text pulled from the PDF keeps the PDF's hard line breaks, so sentences split mid-line in the review box the user must check.
expected: Join wrapped lines into paragraphs before showing the extracted text.
evidence: Extracted text shows 'Wrote and maintained 1,400 regression test cases in TestRail and reviewed every new case' then a new line 'before it shipped.' and 'wrote reproduction steps' then 'engineers could follow.'

what: The launch-film poster is wider than its frame, so route labels at the right edge are cut off, and the play button covers the 'Game...' label on the left.
expected: Poster artwork fits the frame, or the frame crops intentionally with no half-cut labels.
evidence: Visible cut-off labels: 'Forward-Deployed Enginee', 'AI Content Strategi', 'AI Art Direct'; 'Game' label hidden behind the play button.

what: Three statistics with named sources are on the landing page. They could not be checked from here, so they are unverified claims.
expected: Each figure links to its source and the source supports the exact wording (for example '1 in 3 ... laid off in the last two years').
evidence: '1 in 3 U.S. game workers were laid off in the last two years. Source: GDC State of the Game Industry 2026'; '170M new jobs... World Economic Forum'; '62% average pay premium... PwC 2026'.

what: The heading says 'Your map is saved' before any account exists. The map page is already a shareable link without an account, so the wording blurs what is saved and when.
expected: State what the account adds, for example 'Save your map to your account'.
evidence: Heading: 'Your map is saved. Now build the proof.' Body: 'Create your account and your career map comes with you.'

what: Every page logs a CSP violation when a third-party widget script from selfimprove-iota.vercel.app is blocked. Ad and analytics calls to Google and DoubleClick are also refused by the CSP on each page view.
expected: Remove the unused widget reference, or allow it in the CSP; keep console clean of policy errors.
evidence: Console: "Loading the script 'https://selfimprove-iota.vercel.app/widget.js' violates the following Content Security Policy directive"; repeated 'Fetch API cannot load https://www.google.com/...' and 'ad.doubleclick.net' CSP refusals on the landing page.

what: White 'Continue' label on the light green button has low contrast, so the main sign-up action reads weakly.
expected: Button text contrast of at least 4.5:1 (darker green or dark text).
evidence: White text on bright green 'Continue' button in the Clerk widget, same on /sign-in (34-existing-sign-in.png).

what: The assessment page uses a dark theme while the landing, map and Remapped pages are light, so it reads as a different product.
expected: Consistent theme across the public pages, or an intentional and labelled difference.
evidence: Dark background and dark form card on '/assessment/' versus light pages elsewhere.
